conventions.text: argument of periastron of the PRIMARY (Ba), as stated under Table 1; virgil uses the secondary's, = this + 180 deg. Here omega_deg is already virgil's (the paper's primary omega + 180), so omega_shift_deg is 0. 'longitude of ascending node'; which node (approaching or receding) is not stated in the extracted text. virgil's Omega is the PA of the receding node: compare modulo 180 deg until checked

orbit.source: Xuan et al. 2024, Table 1, PMOIRED (frequentist) column; a = a_AU x 173.574 mas/AU (Gaia parallax); omega is virgil's (the paper's primary omega + 180)

caveats: Closure phases only (K band, 2.05-2.38 um): the data are dual-field UT products with no standards in Phase 3, so V² is not used; no calibration template exists for them, so the closure offsets use the loader's widths. Single-night alias peaks of 2024-02-27 and 2024-03-28 are flagged, not fitted (design/orbit_comparison.md section 5). The published orbit uses CRIRES+ radial velocities; ours is astrometry only. The older tile of this target (T1-T5, oidb_fit) stays until this fit is checked.

provenance.data: ~/data/eso_binaries/gravity/oifits/<night>/GRAVI.*_DUAL_SCI_VIS.fits (ESO archive pipeline products, 40 files, 7 nights, UT dual-field wide, MEDIUM; Gl 229 A = HD 42581 on the fringe tracker). Not Phase 3: ivoa.ObsCore holds none of them.
provenance.calibration: virgil-vlti 3395e78: virgil-vlti-calibrate --dual-field --diameter 0.5 --tf-error propagated --bin 1 --window 2.05 2.38 --insname GRAVITY_SC --allow-unrecorded --cp-only-when-uncalibrated; every file closure-phase-only.
